description: Issue #830: the Heritage `value of … for key …` reader must be reachable INSIDE parentheses, which `spec/grammar.md` derives — `primary` (:195-206) offers both `parenthesized-expression` (:201, defined :215) and `value-of-reader` (:205, defined :219), so `( value of :d for key "a" )` is a `parenthesized-expression` wrapping a `value-of-reader`. It once raised `ol-bad-token`: the `(` path took `value` as a `parenthesized-call` callee (:217) and never entered the reader. #885 fixed that incidentally by deriving `NON_PRIMARY_NAMES` from the keyword registry (which contains `value`), so `isCalleeName` rejects it and the `(` path falls through — but nothing pinned it, so a future edit to that derivation would silently restore the defect. This fixture pins the PARSE + SEMANTIC stages clean across every parenthesized shape: the reader wholly parenthesized, as its own dictionary operand, as its own key operand, redundantly grouped, composed with infix `+`, and carrying `.field`/`[selector]` postfixes (proving it is a real `primary`, :194), and both readers parenthesized — two `(`-path fall-throughs in one expression. Its execution twin is `heritage/execution/heritage-value-of-key-reader-in-parentheses`, which runs the same shape set, because `execute()` never calls `check()`. The reader operates on a dict, so Heritage also needs Data (`spec/conformance.md:305`).
